A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlexAvatar and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, references, and supplementary material. Retained content can be matched reliably across appendix reorganization and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original portrait-animation and avatar-creation experiments, component ablations, qualitative comparisons, and fitting-efficiency results in Tables 2–5 and the supplement.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds FaceLift comparisons, targeted fine-tuning and robustness studies, and runtime and memory measurements.

M1.justification: The main architecture, losses, two-token mechanism, and fitting procedure are unchanged. Supplementary Sections B.2 and B.6 add limited experimental adaptations: camera-specific bias tokens and fine-tuning with VOODOOXP expression inputs instead of FLAME codes.

E1.justification: Section B.4 and Figure 14 add evaluation on two challenging lighting conditions using IC-Light example inputs. The original training datasets and four principal tasks remain unchanged; the FaceLift comparisons use the existing Ava256 and in-the-wild head-reconstruction domains.

E2.justification: FaceLift is newly evaluated against FlexAvatar on Ava256 and in-the-wild images in Section A.3, Table 6, and Figures 10–11. Comparator membership in the retained benchmark tables and qualitative comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the experimental designs: a five-subject FaceLift comparison using four frontal and four back cameras with Ava256 excluded from training; fine-tuning with 16 camera-specific bias tokens; varying multi-view data availability; fitting versus no fitting under challenging lighting; and alternative expression controls. The original benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections B.2–B.4 and B.6 add targeted investigations of camera-bias capture, required multi-view data, lighting robustness, and FLAME dependence. These materially expand diagnostic evidence beyond v1's component ablations. The original interpolation and fitting-efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests for these experiments. The additions retain point estimates and qualitative examples without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: New Table 6 reports FlexAvatar/FaceLift PSNR of 17.2/12.8 for frontal views and 15.2/13.2 for back views under the added protocol. Figure 13 reports improved completeness with 1% multi-view data and a complete head at 10%. New camera-token, lighting, expression-control, and resource results substantially extend the evidence. Tables 2–5 and the original fitting-efficiency curves are unchanged.

T1.justification: The method equations and interpolation equations, numbered 1–27, are unchanged. v2 adds empirical demonstrations without new formal assumptions, mathematical derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same claims about complete animatable avatars, bias sinks, the upsampler, and flexible latent-space fitting. The supplementary additions provide supporting evidence without redefining these core contributions.

C2.justification: Section B.2 extends the interpretation of bias sinks to individual camera-subset biases. Section B.4 newly attributes shadow attenuation to evenly lit multi-view training and explains fitting as its remedy. The main limitations remain unchanged, including the now-stale statement that all experiments use FLAME codes.

D1.justification: Section B.5 newly reports 1.7 GB inference VRAM, animation and rendering at 20 fps on an RTX 3090, and two-minute avatar creation including processing. Existing training settings, preprocessing, and access information are retained; the unchanged hyperparameter table moves from Table 6 to Table 7.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to FaceLift and IC-Light. Section A.3 introduces a focused comparison with FaceLift concerning reconstruction completeness, accessories, and animation support. The original related-work discussion and previously cited works are retained.

P1.justification: The main narrative is unchanged apart from citation renumbering and the version stamp. The supplement gains focused subsections, moves fitting-efficiency analysis from B.2 to B.7, updates cross-references, and corrects 'Data Prepaaration' to 'Data Preparation'; existing prose is largely retained.

P2.justification: The supplement adds six figures covering FaceLift comparisons and diagnostic experiments, plus a front/back comparison table, substantially expanding its visual presentation. The previous Figures 10–12 become Figures 16–18, and the hyperparameter table is relocated. Main-paper displays remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The FaceLift comparison and targeted bias-sink, lighting, and expression-control experiments strengthen support for retained claims, while runtime and memory disclosures improve practical assessment. The gains are limited by the small qualitative demonstrations and lack of uncertainty reporting. Section 4.8 also retains an inconsistent claim that all experiments use FLAME despite the new VOODOOXP experiment. Overall, the additions provide useful but bounded improvements to the existing evidence.
